method.unit: Synthetic household; not a real person or contact record
method.marketFirst: Household size 4 or 5; modeled income $75,000–$150,000; income below the Household Living Budget but covering at least 50% of it
method.considerNext: Household size 4 or 5; modeled income $60,000–$175,000; income below the Household Living Budget but covering at least 40% of it; outside the market-first band
method.segments: Market-first households are grouped by young children under 6, school-age members 6–18, or adult-only composition, then split at $110,000 modeled annual income
method.note: Audience tiers support campaign planning only. They are not program eligibility, urgency, or contact permission.

segments.name: Young families building stability
segments.subtitle: Child under 6 · $75K–$110K income
segments.message: Lead with family-sized homes, predictable ownership costs, and a simple first-time-buyer pathway.

segments.name: Growing school-age families
segments.subtitle: Children 6–18 · $75K–$110K income
segments.message: Emphasize stable school communities, enough bedrooms, and purchase support for working families.

topAreas.name: South San Diego / Otay Mesa & South Bay

segments.name: Young families priced out at mid-income
segments.subtitle: Child under 6 · $110K–$150K income
segments.message: Show how below-market pricing and purchase assistance can close the remaining ownership gap.

segments.name: School-age families blocked by prices
segments.subtitle: Children 6–18 · $110K–$150K income
segments.message: Focus on long-term neighborhood stability and the gap between solid income and market home prices.

segments.name: Adult households sharing costs
segments.subtitle: All members 19+ · $75K–$110K income
segments.message: Use first-time-buyer workshops to explain household eligibility, shared purchasing, and unit options.

segments.name: Adult households facing the market gap
segments.subtitle: All members 19+ · $110K–$150K income
segments.message: Lead with the price difference between program homes and the open market, plus financing guidance.
